extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in academic integrity, Serbian politics, and the Siniša Mali plagiarism case
extracted.subtask_short: wiki article on academic plagiarism scandal
extracted.subtask_description: A detailed encyclopedic account of the Siniša Mali doctoral-plagiarism controversy, describing allegations, institutional procedures, commissions' findings, media reactions, and subsequent legal and political fallout. Focus is on how plagiarism was assessed, adjudicated, and sanctioned within Serbian universities and public institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism / non-academic conduct (Article 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of article No. 22 of the university's Code of professional ethics — plagiarism defined as including texts and entire passages in a dissertation without naming the original authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Professional Ethics Board concluded Mali 'literally included texts and entire passages... without naming the original authors' and formally classified this as plagiarism. Examples: 35 pages copied from one dissertation (30 pages >50% copied; 16 nearly complete copies); 51 of 96 footnotes taken from another work without attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage-based assessment of copied material
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of quantitative percentage measures (e.g., '6.97%') as evidence in assessing extent of copying in a thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commissions reported low percentages (6.97%) and deemed them insufficient for sanctions; government media cited figures like 'up to 20% allowed if it's not essential'. The Board carried out detailed page-by-page comparisons and found much higher percentages (e.g., 35 pages copied, many >50%), treating high percentages as strong evidence of plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating circumstances for plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that increase the seriousness of plagiarism beyond isolated citation errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board considered aggravated circumstances such as copying entire passages/pages, adopting another author's references as one's own, inclusion of plagiarized material in conclusions, and large spans of untranslated or unmarked text — these led to describing the plagiarism as 'evident and indisputable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific contribution vs. originality when judging plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between evaluating 'scientific contribution' and determining non-originality/plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Experts Commission argued 'the only important thing is the scientific contribution' and thus dismissed percentage findings; critics noted that scientific contribution is not the metric the commission was formed to judge and that originality and proper attribution are separate standards from contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to compare thesis with other works and present evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation of examining bodies to compare the disputed thesis against source works and include copied passages in reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FON reportedly 'decided not to compare Mali's thesis with other works'; the Board conducted the comparison itself, listing exact pages and demonstrating copied passages. The Board criticized earlier bodies for failing to include copied text and for not establishing complete facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper structuring and admissibility of complaints and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements for complaints and appeals (structure, authorization, deadlines) in university procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mali's lawyers filed complaints citing formalities and procedural defects; the Board found some of his complaints inadmissible (e.g., he argued complainants lacked standing). The rector is authorized to compile complaints; complaints must be properly structured and submitted within procedural deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional roles, powers, and voting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Division of duties and decision-making authorities among faculty commissions, NNV, Ethics Commission/Board, Senate, dean, and rector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: FON's NNV can suggest sanctions but not enforce them (dean must act); Ethics Commission can recommend 'public reprimand' or 'public condemnation'; the Professional Ethics Board can overturn faculty decisions and send matters to the Senate; the Senate's acceptance finalizes annulment of a doctorate. Faculty bodies must follow prescribed procedures (e.g., vote on plagiarism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of judicial review (Administrative Court)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of courts reviewing university plagiarism decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Court may examine technical/procedural aspects but 'can't discuss or revert the merit of the Senate's decision' — it can only return a matter for procedural reasons, not re-evaluate academic merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and justification required in institutional decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions must include clear explanation, description and qualifications of the non-academic behavior they sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board classified the FON's decision as unlawful because it 'lacks clear explanation, description and qualifications of the non-academic behavior'. Bodies must follow previous guidelines and provide full factual bases for conclusions; failure to do so undermines decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions spectrum and their implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of disciplinary outcomes available (public reprimand, public condemnation, admonishment, annulment) and the responsible actors for implementing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Ethics Commission recommended 'public reprimand'; NNV changed recommendation to 'public condemnation'; the dean is charged with making reprimands effective; the Senate can annul a doctorate. The Board reprimanded a dean for failing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality, conflict of interest, and bribery concerns in commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that commissions and voting members act impartially and free from bribery or political pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations included bribery attempts (e.g., claims that Đilas bribed members), pressure from political actors, and accusations that some commissions were politically motivated. The Board criticized commissions for lack of readiness to establish facts and for possible bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic and professional ethics for media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for journalistic behavior and media rhetoric when covering academic controversies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministry of Culture and Information called for strict following of the Serbian Journalists Code and 'generally accepted moral norms', labeling attacks 'unsuitable rhetoric' and 'unacceptable... pejorative, false and incriminating context'. Regulatory Authority for Electronic Media filed charges against broadcasters; journalist associations filed criminal charges against hosts for personal attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standards used to label a finding 'evident and indisputable'
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes sufficiently convincing evidence of plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board's approach: direct textual comparison, identification of specific pages/paragraphs copied, quantification of copied material, showing lack of references/quotation marks, and demonstration that references were appropriated as one's own. When such evidence exists, the Board called the plagiarism 'evident and indisputable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of ghostwriting and its relevance to thesis validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that ghostwriting services exist and that use of ghostwriters undermines thesis authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative reporting indicated a market for ghostwritten theses (minimal price ~€1,000), rapid turnaround, and tailoring to mentors' focus — pointing to structural vulnerabilities in validating genuine authorship and academic integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media accountability for ethnic or personal attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards prohibiting chauvinistic, ethnic, or personally defamatory attacks in media reporting of academic disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Happy TV host attacked professor Sinani on ethnic grounds; regulators and journalist groups filed charges and condemned such attacks as loathing and chauvinistic, indicating regulators expect media to avoid ethnic/name-based attacks and maintain professional standards.
